suggestions.assertion: No new open questions or assumptions are introduced beyond what the draft and the record contain
suggestions.reason: Define 'the record'. The with-skill run's only new assumption is grounded in src/webhook_client.py (a file CLAUDE.md lists under Key Files), which is arguably part of the record even though it is not NOTES.md/CLAUDE.md. As written the assertion fails a well-sourced assumption the same way it would fail an invented one; the author probably wants to catch the latter only. Consider 'every assumption or open question in the edited file traces to the draft, NOTES.md, CLAUDE.md, or a cited project file'.

suggestions.assertion: The chat reply follows the editing-pass report shape: one line, symptom table, one pair, nothing else
suggestions.reason: The assertion bundles the three-element shape with per-element rules (one line, no word count). A reply with the right three elements but a Words row and a three-sentence opener fails it, while a one-line reply with no table would also fail it — the same verdict for very different outputs. Splitting into 'reply is exactly opener + table + one pair' and 'opener is one line and the table carries no word count unless asked' would make the signal discriminating.

No assertion checks that the local-filesystem option is dropped with the replica reason, or that the preamble names a reader. Both are Mode 1 requirements the skill run satisfied and the baseline did not; they would be cheap, discriminating additions.

eval_feedback.overall: Six of eight assertions are discriminating and the skill run passes them cleanly. The two failures are a boundary question (does project source count as 'the record'?) and a strict reading of the report shape; both are near misses the author should decide on rather than clear skill defects.
